messages.subject: ctmm home ranges
parts:
Hi Chris,

 

I am trying to figure out what to do with seasonal home ranges that are larger than the overall home ranges.  I am attaching some figures to help with this.  This is in Mongolia.  The image has 3 home ranges:  all, year 2016, and season 10.  It doesn’t make sense to me that the year and season 10 are large, especially with season 10 as there is a lot of empty space in the home range.  You had mentioned that this could be a sign of movement different from range residency.  But, I am stuck in interpreting this or using another method to calculate the seasonal movement.  Thanks for your help, Nanette.

 

Sent from Mail for Windows 10

messages.author: 40fd627580dd34f5
messages.subject: Re: ctmm home ranges
parts:
Hi Nanette,

The range distribution corresponds to the relative frequencies of everywhere the animal will travel, if it continues the same suite of movement behaviors indefinitely.

Assuming these differences aren't just sampling error... If movement behaviors vary in time, then the range distribution can be larger during one period of time than another, including the full sampling period, which should be intermediate.

When the range distribution is much larger than the sampled data, then this indicates the animal is expected to travel beyond what has currently been sampled, assuming the animal continues the same suite of movement behaviors. In these cases, the effective sample size is very small and the uncertainty is very large.

Best,
Chris
